Michelle —

Thanks for the clear list. I pulled together the high-level answers and attached two artifacts: a sample schema (admin-activity-sample-schema.json) and our export playbook (export-playbook.pdf). Below is a concise overview; happy to jump on a call if you want to walk through the manifest or the snapshot process.

What we log (admin activity snapshot):
- timestamp_utc: ISO8601
- request_id: UUID assigned by the API gateway
- actor: internal user id / service id (redacted per request)
- actor_email: email when available (we can redact at export time)
- actor_role: role at time of action (e.g., admin, billing-rep)
- action: verb (e.g., CREATE_API_KEY, REVOKE_TOKEN, UPDATE_ROUTE_CONFIG)
- target_type: object type (e.g., TOKEN, MODEL, ROUTE)
- target_id: object identifier
- client_ip: source IP (CIDR masked on request)
- user_agent: user agent string
- success: boolean
- status_code: integer HTTP response code
- model_version: model identifier when action affects a deployed model
- region: shard/region where action was executed
- raw_payload_preview: truncated (first 512 bytes) of request body for context

Retention and tiers:
- Hosted API: default 13 months (395 days) retention for admin activity; can export full snapshot at any time.
- Dedicated: default 36 months retention; customer can request extended retention via contract.
- Private (customer-managed): retention is controlled by the customer install; Redwood provides export tooling and recommended retention templates.

Export formats and delivery:
- JSONL (newline-delimited JSON) — recommended for ingestion into Splunk/ELK.
- Compressed tar.gz containing JSONL + manifest.csv + manifest.sha256.sig (detached signature).
- S3: we can deliver a staged snapshot to a customer S3 bucket via cross-account role or provide presigned single-use URLs.
- Streaming: real-time syslog/HTTPS forwarding to customer SIEM for Dedicated and Private deployments (not available for Hosted due to multi-tenant constraints).

Integrity and chain of custody:
- Each snapshot includes a machine-generated manifest with file-level SHA256 checksums and a snapshot-level metadata file (snapshot_id, created_by, created_at, sequence_range).
- Snapshots are signed with Redwood's HSM-backed key (RSA 4096) and we can provide the public key and verification steps.
- We also produce a signed delivery receipt when an export completes (hash + delivery target + timestamp).

Redaction & sampling:
- Redaction: PII fields (actor_email, raw_payload_preview) can be redacted at export time on a per-field basis. Redaction is irreversible for that export; Redwood keeps unredacted copies per retention policy unless customer requests deletion.
- Sampling: We support time-window sampling (e.g., 24-hour slice) and event-sampling (1-in-N). We can also produce deterministic sampling by request-id modulus for reproducibility.

Delivery SLA and timeline:
- Standard snapshot generation for a single region (<= 30 days of logs): 48–72 hours turnaround.
- Large snapshots (months of data or multi-region): 5–10 business days depending on size.
- We provide presigned S3 URLs valid for 72 hours by default; permanent cross-account transfer requires IAM setup (we can provide a CloudFormation role template).

Attached: admin-activity-sample-schema.json (field examples), export-playbook.pdf (playbook and verification steps), delivery_manifest-template.csv (template we populate for each snapshot).

Michelle —

If Acme wants a one-off snapshot to be staged into your S3, here's the operational checklist we typically follow:
1) Customer provides destination bucket ARN and a short-lived cross-account role (we provide a template) OR we provide presigned URLs.
2) We validate IAM permissions and region compatibility (we snapshot in the originating region; cross-region transfer adds an extra step).
3) Snapshot job runs against the admin-activity ledger with sequence numbers. We produce: snapshot_<id>.tar.gz, manifest.csv, manifest.sha256, signature.sig.
4) We upload to the destination and send an email with the manifest and verification steps.

Delivery SLA: once IAM role/permissions are validated, typical delivery for a <= 90-day window is 48 hours; for >90 days or cross-region it's 5 business days.

Cost note: large exports (multi-TB) may incur a one-time processing fee; we'll provide a sizing estimate prior to starting.

Happy to run this for the requested us-west-2 range if you confirm scope.

Thanks,

SRE Lead, Dedicated & Private Deployments
